stem: A public health nurse is assisting with a contact investigation for a client with infectious pulmonary tuberculosis. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Identify people who were exposed while the client could transmit TB, notify and assess those contacts, arrange testing or follow-up as indicated, and protect the index client's identity during notification.
options.B: Tell each contact the index client's name so the contact can personally verify the exposure history before testing.
options.C: Notify only contacts who have already developed symptoms because asymptomatic exposed people do not need assessment.
options.D: Use an unstructured public announcement instead of identifying specific exposed contacts because individual contact assessment has little role in TB control.

rationale: A is correct. CDC describes TB contact investigation as quickly identifying, assessing, and managing people exposed to a person with infectious TB. Contacts are notified that they may have been exposed and may need TB testing and, depending on results, treatment. CDC also states that the index patient's personal and medical information is kept confidential and that contacts are not told the name of the person with active TB disease. B violates that confidentiality principle. C is incorrect because exposed contacts are assessed even if they are asymptomatic. D discards the targeted case-and-contact process used to interrupt transmission.
educational_objective: During a TB contact investigation, identify and evaluate exposed contacts promptly, arrange appropriate testing/follow-up, and preserve the index client's confidentiality rather than disclosing the client's identity to contacts.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Division of Tuberculosis Elimination
source_version_date: CDC page dated March 25, 2024; current page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Contact investigations can help limit the spread of TB: contact tracing is the process of quickly identifying, assessing, and managing people exposed to disease; health departments/contact tracers notify contacts about exposure and precautions/testing. 'The information you share ... is kept confidential': patient information is kept private. 'What to expect if you have been named as a contact': the health care worker tells the contact they may have been exposed but, to maintain privacy/confidentiality, does not tell the name of the person with active TB disease; contacts should obtain TB testing and additional evaluation as indicated.
source_claim_supported: TB contact investigation identifies, notifies, assesses, and manages exposed contacts while protecting the index patient's identity and arranging testing/follow-up even before contacts develop symptoms.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: coordinate referrals and community/public-health resources, maintain confidentiality, and support continuity of care for clients and contacts.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — TB contact investigation and confidentiality
correction_summary: The raw generic contact-tracing item was narrowed to infectious TB so every process and confidentiality claim could be anchored to a current disease-specific CDC source. The final item avoids outdated COVID-era quarantine language and tests targeted contact assessment plus confidentiality.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against CDC's current TB exposure/contact-investigation page rather than relying on archived generic COVID contact-tracing guidance.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects identification, notification, assessment/testing, and confidentiality. B directly contradicts CDC's privacy instruction. C omits asymptomatic exposed contacts. D rejects targeted contact investigation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; the index patient's name is not disclosed to contacts.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; contacts are evaluated because of exposure, not only after symptoms occur.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; targeted contact tracing is a core TB-control strategy.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Specifying infectious TB removes disease-specific differences in contact-management recommendations and leaves A uniquely correct.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern the same contact-investigation workflow.
audit_findings.blueprint: Public-health coordination and confidentiality fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked confidentiality, symptom status, testing, and who performs notification. The item avoids asserting one universal testing method or timing window and does not disclose the index patient's identity. No second answer remained.
